reason: Both material accuracy risks for this naive-FP32 complex division kernel were directly tested on valid in-scope inputs and rebutted. c1 (catastrophic cancellation in FP32 numerators): probe t18 generated 1,107,600 finite FP16 rows with d set to the FP16 grid point nearest -a*c/b or b*c/a (asymmetric cancellation in both real and imaginary numerators), half perturbed by one FP16 ulp — zero violations of the per-component tolerance 1e-7+5e-7*|target|, worst error/tolerance ratio 0.338. c2 (accumulated FP32 roundoff): probe t19 tested 60×131,072 rows spanning FP16 magnitudes with forced no-cancellation signs and skewed denominators (|d|≈|c|·2^-14) — zero violations, worst ratio 0.341. Combined with earlier evidence (t8 extreme-extrema cancellation rows, t9's 200 randomized full-range trials, worst ratio 0.326), the kernel consistently maintains ~3× headroom below the contract tolerance across the decisive worst-case surfaces. Inputs in all probes were finite FP16 [N,2] CUDA tensors passing validate_inputs, exactly the domain problem.txt requires ("EVERY combination of finite FP16 component values is legal ... including both extrema"). The Skeptic reviewed the latest evidence (t22) and recorded no new claims; no open or unresolved claims remain. The kernel's correctly-rounded FP32 division (tl.div_rn) with FP16-exact inputs is sufficient: FP16 products are exact in FP32 in many worst cases, and accumulated roundoff stays well within the 5e-7 relative budget. Verdict: trust.
